name: MonarchDataTable
title: DataTable
wrapsNative: SwiftUI.Table with TableColumnForEach and TableColumn(_:sortUsing:content:) at regular width (iOS 17.4 and later); List with .listStyle(.plain), swipeActions and contextMenu at compact width; Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox) for selection; Menu for row actions and the compact sort
summary: Records in columns: a SwiftUI Table at regular width and a list of records with a labelled line per field at compact width, with sorting, selection, row actions, column visibility and order, and the loading, empty, filtered and error states.
whenToUse: For a screen of records with several fields each (tickets, invoices, people) that people scan, sort, select and act on, on iPhone and iPad.
whenNotToUse: For records with one or two fields, use a List. For a list fetched page by page with no columns, use MonarchCursorList. For a small fixed table inside a document, use MonarchTableBlock.
api: init(_ caption: String, rows: [Row], columns: [MonarchDataTableColumn<Row>], sort: Binding<MonarchDataTableSort?>? = nil, selection: Binding<Set<Row.ID>>? = nil, hiddenColumns: Set<String> = [], columnOrder: [String] = [], layout: MonarchDataTableLayout = .automatic, sortsRows: Bool = true, isLoading: Bool = false, errorMessage: String? = nil, isFiltered: Bool = false, footer: MonarchLoadMore? = nil, labels: MonarchDataTableLabels = MonarchDataTableLabels(), rowLabel: ((Row) -> String)? = nil, isRowSelectable: ((Row) -> Bool)? = nil, rowActions: ((Row) -> [MonarchDataTableRowAction])? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onClearFilters: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onOpen: (@MainActor (Row) -> Void)? = nil) where Row: Identifiable

MonarchDataTableColumn<Row>.init(_ title: String, id: String? = nil, isNumeric: Bool = false, isSortable: Bool = true, isHideable: Bool = true, width: CGFloat? = nil, value: @escaping @Sendable (Row) -> String, sortBy: (@Sendable (Row, Row) -> Bool)? = nil)
MonarchDataTableRowAction.init(_ title: String, id: String? = nil, systemImage: String? = nil, isDestructive: Bool = false, isDisabled: Bool = false, action: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void)
enum MonarchDataTableLayout { case automatic, table, list }

struct MonarchDataTableLabels { var selectAll, actionsHeader, openHint, sort, sortedAscending, sortedDescending, noValue, loading, emptyTitle, emptyMessage, filteredTitle, filteredMessage, errorTitle, retry: String?; var selectRow, rowActions: (@Sendable (String) -> String)?; var selectedCount: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? }

options.name: caption
options.description: Names the table for VoiceOver, such as "Open tickets".

options.name: rows
options.description: The rows, in the app's order.

options.name: columns
options.description: Every column in its default order: header, cell text, numeric alignment, sort rule, whether it sorts and hides, ideal width.

options.name: sort
options.description: The sort, one column and a direction. nil keeps the sort inside the table, starting unsorted.

options.name: selection
options.description: The selected ids. With it, rows get checkboxes and a select-all checkbox appears above them.

options.name: hiddenColumns
options.description: Ids of hidden columns, as MonarchColumnChooser writes them.

options.name: columnOrder
options.description: Column ids in display order; missing ids follow in their default order.

options.name: layout
options.description: A table at regular width and a list at compact width or the accessibility text sizes, or always one of them.

options.name: sortsRows
options.description: Whether the table sorts rows itself; false when the server sorts and the app reloads on sort changes.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: With no rows, shows placeholder rows; with rows, the footer shows progress.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: With no rows, shows the error state with this message.

options.name: isFiltered
options.description: No rows means the filters matched nothing: the filtered empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: A load-more footer under the rows, for paged data.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: rowLabel
options.description: A row's name in spoken labels. By default the first shown column's text.

options.name: isRowSelectable
options.description: Whether a row has a checkbox.

options.name: rowActions
options.description: A row's actions: an actions menu, the context menu and, in the list, swipe and VoiceOver actions.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds Retry to the error state.

options.name: onClearFilters
options.description: Adds Clear filters to the filtered state.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Opens a row: the row's name (table) or the whole record (list) becomes a button.

states.name: table
states.description: A system Table with a checkbox column, the shown columns with sortable headers, and an actions column.

states.name: list
states.description: One record per row: checkbox, the name in bold (link-coloured when it opens), a "Field value" line per other column, and an actions menu; a Sort menu sits above the rows.

states.name: selected
states.description: Checked checkboxes and "3 selected" beside Select all rows.

states.name: loading
states.description: With no rows, a MonarchLoadingState of rows named "Loading rows".

states.name: failed
states.description: With no rows, a MonarchErrorState, "These rows could not be loaded", with the message and Retry.

states.name: filtered
states.description: A filtered MonarchEmptyState, "No rows match these filters", with Clear filters.

appearance: The table and list are the system's, on the screen background. Cell text uses the default text role, field names, counts and empty cells (a dash) the muted role, an openable row name the link role, destructive actions the system destructive style. Checkboxes are the Monarch checkbox style. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes come from these roles.
platformNotes: SwiftUI's Table shows only its first column at compact width, so Monarch supplies the compact row; at regular width the table is the system Table, whose dynamic columns need iOS 17.4 (on 17.0 to 17.3 the list is shown). Cells are text from each column's value; the web's custom cell renderers, expandable rows, column resizing, multi-column sort, keyboard grid navigation, pagination and select-all-matching are not offered: use a footer MonarchLoadMore for paging and let the app widen columns with width. Every column of the system Table can be clicked to sort, so a column that is not sortable ignores the request and keeps the current sort. Selection is a checkbox column and a select-all checkbox, not the system's edit-mode selection, so it works the same in both layouts. The web density option has no equivalent; rows use the system heights. Android uses the same name and options. Several closures are optional (rowLabel, isRowSelectable, rowActions, onRetry, onClearFilters, onOpen). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is rowLabel.
accessibility: The table or list is named by caption.
In the list layout each record is one element read as "Ticket 42, Status: Open, Owner: Ana Lima", with "No value" for empty cells; with onOpen it is a button with the hint "Opens the details".
Row actions are VoiceOver actions on the record, and also a separate menu button named "Actions for" and the row's name.
Each checkbox is named "Select" and the row's name; Select all rows is a checkbox with the selected count beside it.
The compact Sort menu reads the sorted column and "sorted ascending" or "sorted descending" as its value.
In the table layout the system reads headers and cells; empty cells read "No value".
At the accessibility text sizes the automatic layout is the list, and field names stack above their values.
edgeCases: The default sort compares cell texts as Finder does ("Item 9" before "Item 10"); pass sortBy for grouped numbers, dates and amounts.
Sorting is stable: equal rows keep the app's order.
Hidden columns that cannot be hidden stay shown.
Select all only adds and removes the selectable rows on screen; other selected ids are kept.
Both layouts fill their space and scroll; do not nest the table in a ScrollView.

examples.title: Sorting, selection, row actions and grid keyboard
examples.webExample: Sorting, selection, row actions and grid keyboard
examples.template:
MonarchDataTable(
    {{caption}},
    rows: invoices,
    columns: [
        MonarchDataTableColumn({{columns.0.header}}, id: {{columns.0.id}}, isHideable: false, value: { $0.customer }),
        MonarchDataTableColumn(
            {{columns.1.header}},
            id: {{columns.1.id}},
            value: { $0.status },
            tone: { invoice in
                switch invoice.status {
                case "Paid": .success
                case "Overdue": .danger
                default: .neutral
                }
            }
        ),
        MonarchDataTableColumn({{columns.2.header}}, id: {{columns.2.id}}, value: { $0.issued }),
        MonarchDataTableColumn({{columns.3.header}}, id: {{columns.3.id}}, value: { $0.owner }),
        MonarchDataTableColumn(
            {{columns.4.header}},
            id: {{columns.4.id}},
            isNumeric: true,
            value: { $0.amount.formatted(.currency(code: "USD").precision(.fractionLength(0)).locale(Locale(identifier: "en_US"))) },
            sortBy: { $0.amount < $1.amount }
        ),
    ],
    sort: $sort,
    selection: $selection,
    rowActions: { _ in
        [
            MonarchDataTableRowAction({{rowActions.0}}) {},
            MonarchDataTableRowAction({{rowActions.1}}, isDestructive: true) {},
        ]
    },
    onOpen: { _ in }
)
.frame(height: 480)
